title: Python Foundations
promise: Build small Python programs while understanding every decision.

modules.title: Values and names
modules.mental_model: A variable is a readable name attached to a value so you can use or change that value later.
evidence: assigns a value to a meaningful name
uses the name in a later expression
common_mistakes: uses a name before assigning it
understanding_checks: What value does this name hold now?

modules.title: Making decisions
modules.mental_model: A condition is a yes-or-no question that lets Python choose which instructions to run.
evidence: explains which branch runs for an example input
understanding_checks: What question is Python answering here?
Which branch runs for this value, and why?

modules.title: Collections and repetition
modules.mental_model: A collection holds related values; a loop asks Python to repeat the same instructions for each value.
evidence: places repeated work inside the loop
common_mistakes: puts repeated work outside the loop
resets a total or collection inside the loop
understanding_checks: What does the loop variable hold each time?
Which value must survive between repetitions?

modules.title: Reusable responsibilities
modules.mental_model: A function gives one responsibility a name, accepts the information it needs, and can return a result.
common_mistakes: defines but never calls the function
prints when the caller needs a returned value

modules.title: Programs that meet the real world
modules.mental_model: Real programs receive imperfect input; they need clear boundaries for reading data, handling expected failure, and organizing reusable code.
evidence: reads or writes a file safely
understanding_checks: Which errors should this code handle?
What belongs outside the source code?
